skill.name: azure-storage-file-share-ts
skill.description: Use @azure/storage-file-share with TypeScript or JavaScript to manage Azure File Shares, directories, files, metadata, snapshots, and SAS access.
skill.summary: Guides TypeScript and Node.js users through Azure File Share SDK operations.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static command and network alerts are false positives from Markdown fences, TypeScript template literals, and Azure SDK endpoint examples. Real security-sensitive content remains around credential-bearing environment variables and local file reads used for Azure file upload workflows. No prompt injection attempt was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Credential-bearing examples use connection strings, account keys, and SAS tokens.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer DefaultAzureCredential in primary examples, and warn users not to print or expose secret environment variables.

remediation.issue: Local file upload examples read paths from the user machine.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to confirm exact local paths and destination shares before upload or download operations.

remediation.issue: The share SAS example grants broad permissions for 24 hours.
remediation.suggestion: Show least privilege permissions, shorter expirations, and separate examples for read-only and write-only access.

content.user_title: Manage Azure File Shares with TypeScript
content.value_statement: Azure File Share workflows often need precise SDK patterns for authentication, uploads, downloads, and share management. This skill provides focused TypeScript and JavaScript guidance using @azure/storage-file-share.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to install @azure/storage-file-share and @azure/identity for Node.js projects.
Explains connection strings, shared keys, DefaultAzureCredential, and SAS token authentication.
Covers creating, listing, deleting, and configuring Azure File Shares.
Documents directory and file operations, including upload, download, copy, metadata, and ranges.
Includes snapshot handling, SAS generation, error handling, and TypeScript type references.
Compares Node.js and browser support for SDK features.
limitations: It does not provision Azure accounts, storage accounts, or network access.
Examples require valid Azure credentials and permissions from the user environment.
Code samples need adaptation and testing before production use.
It does not replace security review for data handling or access policies.

use_cases.title: Build File Share Integrations
use_cases.description: Use SDK patterns to add Azure File Share uploads, downloads, and metadata operations to a TypeScript service.

use_cases.title: Automate Storage Operations
use_cases.description: Create repeatable scripts for share creation, quota changes, snapshots, and cleanup tasks.

use_cases.title: Review Azure Storage Access
use_cases.description: Compare authentication options and SAS scopes before implementing access to shared files.

prompt_templates.title: Connect to Azure Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to connect to Azure File Share from Node.js using environment variables and the recommended Azure SDK client.

prompt_templates.title: Upload and Download Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a TypeScript workflow to upload a local file, download it later, and handle missing shares or files safely.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Safer SAS Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a least privilege SAS plan for one Azure file with a short expiration and clear permissions.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Production Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Azure File Share plan for large files, streaming, metadata, snapshots, error handling, and secret handling.

output_examples.input: A developer asks how to authenticate a Node.js service to Azure Files.
output: Explains connection strings and shared keys for local development.
Identifies which client type starts each storage workflow.

output_examples.input: An engineer needs a safe upload and download plan for large files.
output: Uses streaming for large uploads and downloads.
Adds confirmation points for local paths and Azure destinations.

output_examples.input: A platform team wants temporary access to one file.
output: Chooses a file-scoped SAS instead of a broad share token.
Limits permissions to the required operation.
Uses a short expiration and records the intended audience.

best_practices: Use managed identity through DefaultAzureCredential for production workloads when possible.
Confirm source paths, destination shares, and permissions before file transfer or delete operations.
Use least privilege SAS permissions with short expirations and clear ownership.
anti_patterns: Do not paste account keys, connection strings, or SAS tokens into prompts or logs.
Do not grant broad share SAS permissions when one file operation is enough.
Do not run delete or overwrite examples without confirming the exact target.

faq.question: Does this skill manage Azure File Shares directly?
faq.answer: No. It provides SDK guidance and examples. The user or agent must run adapted code with valid Azure access.

faq.question: Which languages does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers JavaScript and TypeScript usage with @azure/storage-file-share for Node.js and browser contexts.

faq.question: Can it help with authentication choices?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains connection strings, shared keys, DefaultAzureCredential, and SAS tokens with platform notes.

faq.question: Does it include local file transfer examples?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows upload and download patterns, including Node.js file paths and streams.

faq.question: Can it generate SAS token guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents file and share SAS generation, but users should reduce permissions and expiration times.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production without changes?
faq.answer: No. Review credentials, permissions, error handling, and data handling before using any sample in production.
